To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the P2x2 and P2x4 protein levels were not altered in P2x2 knockout (P2X6-/-) mouse kidneys and heart.
P2x6 KO mice do not show any significant difference in electrolyte homeostasis compared to WT mice.
the P2X6 receptor is not involved in the regulation electrolyte homeostasis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of a P2X6 knockout mouse line.
the development of P2X receptor agonists and antagonists as therapeutic tools in renal diseases.
the development of P2x knockout mice and the analysis of renal expression of other P2X subunits, electrolyte transporters and P2X2/4 in P2x knockout animals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
P2X6 plays a role in electrolyte homeostasis under certain conditions, e.g. during pathophysiological states.
the P2X6 receptor is not involved in the regulation renal ion transport.
P2X6 plays a minor role in renal electrolyte handling and that compensatory effects are not apparent in P2x2, P2x4 and other electrolyte transporters in kidney and heart.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we generated P2x6 KO mice and we found no differences in electrolyte handling in these animals.
P2X6 knockout mice do not exhibit a significant phenotype and that the P2X6 receptor is not involved in the regulation or maintenance of renal electrolyte homeostasis.
P2x6 is not a major contributor in the regulation of electrolyte handling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
P2X6 does not play a significant role in electrolyte handling in mouse kidney under normal physiological conditions.
P2X6 may be involved in electrolyte transport in a tissue-specific manner.
